Subject: Draft Mutual Action Plan + next steps (Helios Capital)

Hi Tom / Elena —

Great to meet you both on the call earlier. Attached is the first-pass Mutual Action Plan ("MAP") based on today's discovery: Helios's priority is to validate latency and cost predictability for the private deployment path, with procurement and security signoffs as the main gating items.

Summary (short):
- Target close date (initial): 2026-12-15
- Pilot (technical eval) start: 2026-11-29 — 2 weeks
- Procurement / legal review window: 2026-12-06 to 2026-12-13
- Go/no-go + purchase order: 2026-12-15

Key responsibilities (draft):
- Helios: provide sample PII-redacted dataset + security questionnaire (Elena)
- Redwood: deliver environment runbook & pilot config (Marcus)
- Workspace/Contract: procurement point-of-contact and estimated PO timing (Tom)

Dependencies / open items:
- SOC 2 evidence — Helios to confirm acceptable artifacts by 11/30
- Network peering window (approx 24–72 hrs) once VPC details are shared

Asks for you both: please review the attached MAP and call out any milestone that needs to move or an owner that should change. If the dates look good, can we lock a 30-minute follow-up next Tue (11/23) to finalize milestones and confirm the legal intake path?

Attachments: Helios_MAP_v1.xlsx (map with milestones, owners, dates)

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

— Rachel

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the clear recap and the MAP. Quick update from our side after internal alignment: procurement has a heavier backlog than expected and legal has one required data-flow diagram to produce before they start their review. Practically that means our target decision date needs to move out. Proposed adjustments:

- Move target close to 2027-01-27 (end of January)
- Pilot start can still be week of 11/29, but we need to shorten the pilot scope to the core latency/cost tests only (remove user-scaling scenarios for now)
- Procurement will prioritize the PO once legal confirms the diagram; I expect diagram to be ready by 12/10

I've attached a marked-up copy of your MAP with revised dates and a short note on scope "Option A (core)" vs "Option B (full)." Can Redwood confirm whether the shortened pilot still gives us the latency signals we need? Also, are you able to pause the billing clock during the additional procurement wait (we may ask for a small credit if the decision slips past 12/15)?

Happy to discuss on a quick call — Tom and I are available 11/24 or 11/30 in the afternoons.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Director, Infrastructure Risk | Helios Capital
elena.rossi@helioscap.com

Folks — quick internal + customer-facing note. Elena just confirmed procurement/legal push; she asked to move the decision window to 2027-01-27 and to run a narrowed pilot focused on latency/cost profiling.

Proposed internal approach (can we align by EOD):
1) Accept revised target close: move to 2027-01-27 in the MAP. (Owner: Rachel)
2) Shortened Pilot (Option A): two 48-hr runs on customer sample traffic with fixed concurrency to capture tail latency and token cost. (Owner: Marcus)
3) Pause billing / provide trial credit for procurement delay: offer a 2-week credit after pilot start if Helios is still in procurement by 12/15. (Owner: Priya / Finance)
4) Security artifacts: prioritize sending the redacted KV/systems diagram to Elena by 11/30 to unblock legal. (Owner: Neha)
5) Update MAP and send revised MAP v1.1 to Helios with the new dates and scope (Owner: Rachel)

Action items / next steps:
- Marcus: can you confirm that Option A (2 x 48-hr runs) will produce the latency and cost signals Elena needs? If not, recommend minimum add-back.
- Neha: can you own the SOC2 artifact packet + coordinate the network diagram with their architect?
- Priya: please confirm whether Finance can approve the proposed small trial credit and the mechanism (credit vs invoice hold).

I will update the MAP and propose 11/30 1:00pm ET for a quick alignment call with the Helios procurement/legal group (Elena said 11/30 afternoons work).

Cc'ing Tom/Elena so they can see we are moving fast on the ask.

— Rachel
